Per: Justice Anand Pathak The instant Writ Appeal under Section 2(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Uchcha Nyayalaya (Khand Nyayapeeth Ko Appeal) Adhiniyam, 2005 is filed being aggrieved by the order dt.21.07.2025 passed by the learned Writ Court in W.P.No.26347/2025, whereby the writ petition filed by the appellant (petitioner) was dismissed.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Grievance of the appellant is that vide order dated 23.08.2021, she was transferred from Guna and was posted at Morena.
She actively participated in the campaign of preventing food adulteration in District Morena.
Due to pressure of mafia involved in food adulteration, she has been transferred.
Due to transfer of the petitioner, her entire family is suffering.
Appellant submitted representation to respondent No.2 on 27.06.2025 but of no avail.
Hence, she approached Writ Court by filing W.P.No.26347/2025.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16069 2 WA-2205-2025 3.

The Writ Court after considering the facts and circumstances of the case, dismissed the writ petition filed by the petitioner by impugned order holding therein that no ground is made out for interference in the transfer order on the ground of malafide raised by the petitioner.

It has further Smt Kiran Sengar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39574613/
1 been held that the transfer order cannot be interfered with based upon personal inconvenience of the petitioner as also on the ground of violation of transfer policy.
4 .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Writ Court did not appreciate the facts of the case and passed the impugned order even without considering Clause 52 of the Transfer Policy.
Appellant has been transferred at the instance of food adulteration mafia as the petitioner was taking action against the said mafia.

Appellant submitted representation against the transfer order,
but of no avail.
Learned Writ Court did not consider the aforesaid facts properly and passed the impugned order, which is liable to be set aside.
5 . Respondent/State supported the impugned order and prayed for dismissal of appeal.

6 . Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended thereto.
7.
Transfer is an incident of service.
No one much less appellant has any vested right to be posted at a particular place of posting.

It is well settled in law that employer is the best judge to organize its work force and it is also well settled in law that a transfer order cannot be subjected to judicial review unless and until same is found to be influenced by mala fide or arbitrary NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16069 3 WA-2205-2025 exercise of powers which petitioner/appellant fails to do so.
Concept of equality as enshrined under Articles 14 and 16 of Constitution of India, has no application to the cases of transfers.

8 . This is a case where appellant, who is working as Food Inspector Grade - II, is aggrieved by the order vide order dt.30.05.2025, whereby she has been transferred from the office of Deputy Director, Food & Medicine Administration, Morena to the office of Deputy Director, Food &
Medicine Administration, Bhind on administrative ground.
9. Sheet anchor of the argument of the appellant is that because of the influence of food mafia she has been transferred from Morena to Bhind.
Appellant raised the ground that she was doing good work in compliance of the order passed by this Court Contempt Case No.248/2021.

Said contempt petition was in fact filed for non-compliance of orders passed by this Court in PIL preferred by one Umesh Kumar Bohare (W.P.No.15328/2019), in which directions were issued and when directions were not complied with, then contempt petition was filed.

Therefore, filing of contempt petition itself shows that authorities including appellant were not vigilant enough to perform their duties as Food Safety Officers and when wrath of contempt proceedings stared them, then they tried to save their skin.
10.
If 105 samples are taken by the appellant between January to June 2025, then question arises what she was doing prior to this period.
Whether she felt duty bound to do her duties to curb rampant business of preparation of adulterated spurious milk (Urea based milk) and other adulterated items prepared from milk and other chemicals.
Petitioner as per her own NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16069 4 WA-2205-2025 submissions, is posted at Morena since 2021 and she already completed four years over said post.
Prior to it, her performance nowhere suggests any pro active steps taken by her to protect the common man from adulterated food stuff.

Smt Kiran Sengar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39574613/
2

entities.text: Smt Kiran Sengar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, under administrative exigencies as mentioned by the respondents, and duly noted by the learned Writ Court, if she is transferred from Morena to Bhind, then it can not be interfered with on the ground of malice or on the ground that transfer has been made at the instance of food mafia.
11. In fact, Morena and Bhind are neighbouring districts and therefore no personal inconvenience can be caused to the appellant if she is posted at Bhind.
Therefore, personal ground raised on personal inconvenience also deserves to be rejected at the threshold.
12. So far as ground taken by the appellant regarding long retention of other Food Officers in District Morena is concerned, it is definitely for the respondents/State to look after this aspect.
Respondent/State shall have to see that Morena, Bhind and Gwalior area are all adjoining area suffering from menace of adulterated food stuff specially food items prepared from milk.
It is causing serious threat to the life and health of common citizen residing in this area.
Still State Govt.
has not taken any pro active steps to check this menace.
13. Food Safety Officers are not pro actively performing their duties to regularly check adulterated food or punishing perpetrators.

This is a serious concern, which deserves to be conveyed to the respondent/State to look into it and take pro active steps as per letter and spirit of orders passed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16069 5 WA-2205-2025 in W.P.No. 15328/2019 (PIL) and Contempt Case No.248/2021.
14.
However, appellant can not get the benefit of prevailing menace of food adulteration in this area if others are retained and appellant is removed.
15. As discussed in preceding paras, respondents/State shall ensure compliance of this order.

16. From the perusal of grounds raised by the appellant and the discussion surfaced in the impugned order, it appears that appeal is misconceived and the appellant/petitioner is trying to retain herself somehow at Morena by showing the fact that she collected 105 samples during preceding six months.
That is her duty which is to be performed wherever she is posted.

Therefore, appeal is misconceived and is hereby dismissed with cost of Rs.25,000/- (Rs. Twentyfive Thousand Only) to be deposited in favour of Juvenile Justice Fund having Saving Bank Account No.60411029562 of Bank of Maharashtra, Branch Govindpura, Bhopal, IFSC Code MAHB0001988 within one month.

1 7 . A copy of this order be sent to respondents specially Principal Secretary, Public Health and Medical Education and the Commissioner, Food Safety Department, Idgah Hills, Bhopal for information and compliance of this order.

(ANAND PATHAK) (HIRD  JUDGE JUD  SP Smt Kiran Sengar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39574613/
